newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SFE wheat futures stay tradeless, back months low.
newsitem.headline: SFE wheat futures stay tradeless, back months low.

text.p: Sydney Futures Exchange wheat futures had another tradeless day on Thursday before the Easter break, while settlement quotes drifted.

Brendan Hillary of ANZ Futures Ltd said the Australian market had been drifting higher with Chicago, which was dominated by fund activity. Hillary does not see wheat entering a fundamentally bullish phase.

The market was underpinned by expectations of a smaller U.S. spring wheat crop, he said. But the winter wheat crop looked the best in ten years and should more than make up for declines in the spring crop.

Another factor in the market was expected flooding when snow north of the U.S. spring wheat areas melted. Flooding in the next month would not cause a problem but flooding after that could delay the spring wheat planting, he said.
The market contained some risk premium on this, he said.

CBOT wheat futures presently carried a A$10.00-A$15.00 premium on Australian wheat futures in the back months. This could produce more activity in the Australian back months closer to U.S. planting, he said.
A rise to A$180.00 a tonne by January 1998 would create enormous grower interest in hedging, he said.
